narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Stage and the Controller"**

PopQuiz is warm muted and light, built for a room. The host screen is a stage read from the back row: one idea per screen, the question at display size, a full-width timer bar, and four answer tiles filling the lower half that carry their own counts at reveal, so the whole stage fits one viewport. The phone is a controller held in one hand: the tiles become big tap targets and after reveal the whole page fills olive or terracotta with the verdict. Everything else (landing, dashboard, editor, reports, auth) is parchment ground with warm charcoal ink and slightly lighter surfaces, so the color budget is spent where the game happens.

The ground is flat. 1px rules divide headers and lists, surfaces sit a half-step lighter than the ground, and one soft lift is the only shadow. Saturated color lives in two places: terracotta for the single action on a screen, and the answer quartet. The quartet always carries its shape, so color is never the only signal. Motion has one grammar: things rise or grow into place from an already-visible state on one expo ease, and reduced motion turns it off.

The build rejects the purple-confetti game show and the SaaS card grid. Light theme only; the palette is the user's "Warm muted" choice.
keyCharacteristics: Parchment ground, warm charcoal ink, near-white surfaces, 1px warm rules.
Terracotta is the one action color; the quartet (terracotta triangle, dusty teal diamond, ochre circle, olive square) is the one moment of full saturation.
DM Sans throughout, bold and tight (-0.03em) for headings; DM Mono only for PINs, timers and IDs.
Flat surfaces with a single soft lift, 14px tiles, 12-16px controls.
The host stage scales its root font with the viewport; every rem on it scales, 1280x720 to 4K.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: A screen has one terracotta button. Secondary actions are quiet (surface, rule), dark (ink) or ghost.

rules.name: The Quartet Travels Together Rule
rules.body: The quartet appears as a set, in the fixed order triangle, diamond, circle, square, and a quartet color never shows up without its shape. Outside the game it appears only in the brand mark, the verdict pages, and data bars.

rules.name: The Reveal Drains Rule
rules.body: After reveal, wrong tiles fall back to sunken with muted ink and an ink/15 fill bar; only the correct tile keeps its color, a check, and a white/45 fill bar.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Codes Rule
rules.body: DM Mono only sets PINs, the timer and IDs. Scores, ranks and counts are DM Sans with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes live (score, timer, answered count, tile counts, PIN) uses tabular-nums so it does not jitter.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: h1 to h3 balance their wrap and track at -0.03em.

rules.name: The One Viewport Stage Rule
rules.body: The host stage sets its root font to clamp(16px, min(1.25vw, 2.2vh), 48px) and on screens at least 1024x600 (the `stage` variant) locks to h-dvh with no page scroll; shorter or narrower screens scroll, and the question view scrolls inside itself only when long content needs it, so one layout fits 1280x720 through 4K. Vertical sizes on the stage use vh-aware clamps (tile min-height clamp(4rem, 13vh, 7rem), podium blocks min(14rem, 30vh) / min(10rem, 22vh) / min(7rem, 15vh)). Reveal counts live inside the tiles rather than in a separate chart, so the stage never needs a second screen. Below lg the stage scrolls and the tile grid drops to one column under sm.

rules.name: The Short Rule
rules.body: On landscape screens under 500px tall (the `short` variant), answers go to one row of four (two for true/false), tiles drop their min-height and shrink their shape and text, and verdict type steps down.

rules.name: The Coarse Pointer Rule
rules.body: On coarse pointers every small control grows to a 44px target (lobby kick buttons to 40px with negative margin, connect-panel ghost buttons to 44px, dashboard quiz links gain block padding, auth fields and buttons to 44px).

rules.name: The Narrow Wordmark Rule
rules.body: Under 380px the wordmark keeps only the mark; the name stays for screen readers.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: There is one shadow. Admin cards and surfaces stay flat with a border; only tappable or stage objects lift.

rules.name: The Shared Rank Rule
rules.body: Equal score is equal rank: rank is the position of the first player with that score, and ordinals print the shared rank (two "1st", then "3rd"). Podium order is 2nd, 1st, 3rd, but block height follows rank, so tied players stand level; rank 1 blocks are terracotta, the rest ink. Blocks grow up in sequence (3rd, 2nd, 1st).

dos: Do keep one terracotta primary per screen and drop everything else to quiet, dark or ghost.
Do pair every quartet color with its shape, in the fixed order terracotta triangle, teal diamond, ochre circle, olive square.
Do set ink text on ochre and white text on terracotta, teal and olive.
Do use fired terracotta, not terracotta, for text on the terracotta wash.
Do size host-stage type and spacing in rem or em so the stage root scale carries them, and size stage heights with vh-aware clamps.
Do give every control on coarse pointers a 44px target.
Do use tabular figures for every live number, and DM Mono only for PINs, timers and IDs.
Do animate only with rise, grow-up, grow-x or pop on the expo-out ease (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), from an already-visible state, and honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't add a second shadow, or lift admin cards; they stay flat with a 1px rule.
Don't introduce a dark theme, gradients, or a purple game-show palette.
Don't set stage text in fixed px; it breaks the one-viewport scaling.
Don't break ties by list position; tied scores share the rank and the podium height.
Don't pull in an icon library; add paths to the authored 24px, 1.75-stroke set.
